why: The best entry this project has, pinned so it cannot be lost to a roster edit or a kernel rewrite. Every field here was READ from the run that scored, not composed afterwards: the kit commit comes from the kernel log's own 'kit <sha>' line, the members from the kernel's `chosen` tuple, the board score from the submissions API. `python -m kneemri.kaggle.champion_check` is what keeps it true.
kernel_owner_why: The `kernel` field is a LOCAL directory name — `comp/kernels/<kernel>/<kernel>.py` — and the Kaggle API wants `<owner>/<kernel>`, which is not derivable from it. The owner slug here is NOT the git/Kaggle account name the repo is under (`dimiturtrz`); it is `dimiturnt`, and asking for the wrong one returns `Permission 'kernels.get' was denied`, which reads as an auth failure rather than a typo. Cost a round on 2026-09-08. Read it from `kaggle kernels list --mine -s kneemri` if it ever changes.

serving.vote: LogitAverage for our seven, then RaptorSeat rank blend at 2/3 for the foreign wave
serving.foreign_seat: The public 0.950 wave, NOT packaged by comp/members.roster: nartaa's CoAtNet (nartaa/rsna-knee-publication-swa-weights-20261007, served by nartaa's own scoring cell mounted from dimiturnt/nartaa-mirror-src) rank-blended per finding with goodpjw2008's ConvNeXt reader (goodpjw2008/rsna-knee-2-5d-convnext-reader, Apache-2.0, its own infer.py) at rabari9999's V1 shares. Rebuilt by Kaggle mounts on the pinned pre-2026-10-09 image (docker_image in kernel-metadata).

principles: A THIRD FAMILY OVER THE PUBLIC WAVE IS WORTH TWO TICKS, and this is the first pin to sit above the public frontier rather than below it. triseat_v1 is the public 0.950 blend (nartaa CoAtNet + goodpjw ConvNeXt reader, per-finding shares found on the public board) with tripleseat's seven seated at 1/3 of a final rank blend. It read 0.952 against the wave's 0.950 (444 teams tied there) and ours7's 0.945, the top of its pre-registered '>= 0.952 adds' band, rank 129 of 5567 at 10:07Z. Both public arms trained on every labelled study, so this entry has NO offline number and the 1/3 share was named before the read, not fitted. Two ticks is directional against the 1.5% bar; what it establishes is that our DINO/ResNet family carries error structure the CoAtNet/ConvNeXt lineage every public notebook shares does not.

THE PIN MOVED FOR ONE RESOLVABLE STEP, AND ONLY ONE. tripleseat_v2 is stackseat_v1 with its two weakest seats (grade_ladder_cf, lr4e-5_ws_cf) out and three labelwise drop40_long fold-0 bases in, raptor at 1/3 and LogitAverage held, seven of ours. It read 0.946 against 0.944 - +0.002, one step past BOARD_RESOLVABLE = 0.0015 and inside its pre-registered 0.9455-0.9469 'real gain' band, the first read to leave the flat 0.944 band three designed entries sat in. The fold-0-twin proxy projected ~+0.0084; about a quarter landed, so the proxy's SIGN transferred and its SIZE did not. Directional under the 1.5% bar. run_check read 7 of 7 before the pin moved.

THE PIN MOVED SIDEWAYS FOR A LICENCE, NOT FOR A SCORE, and that is the only reason it moved. raptorweight_v1 and this entry BOTH read 0.944 - an exact tie, not a tick - and they differ in one seat: merged_blend_cf, whose training table is the Rijeka external expert read whose terms are unresolved against competition rule 2.5, is replaced by stack_increments_ff, fitted on blend_three_v1.csv (our own table averaged with two public LLM readers by core.data.labels.table_blend - no Rijeka). champion_check's LICENCE EXPOSURE warning names the remedy in as many words: a clean entry that ties it replaces it. `licence_refusals` over this entry's seven seats returns NONE. Everything else is byte-identical to the previous pin - same count, same order, same overlap=False, same LogitAverage, same raptor checkpoint at 1/3, same rank-space join - so nothing in the list below is repriced by this move, and NO board delta may be argued from it. It cost zero submission slots, which is the whole point: rule 2.5 binds the WINNING submission, so the exposure had to be cleared before a result was won under it, not after.

ALL-OURS NO LONGER BEATS GRAFTED, AND THIS ENTRY IS WHY. The principle below it was fitted on a graft of twenty CC0 members of UNKNOWN and mostly poor quality, which is a statement about THOSE members and was read as one about grafting. raptor_v4_swa scored 0.923 solo on the board, EXACTLY level with our own best single (calibsolo 0.923) on the same day, and seating it seventh at 1/7 took 0.941 to 0.943. Member quality held equal to three decimals; the only variables were the architecture, the decode and the training corpus. Read the old principle as bounded to weak grafts.

THE POOL IS AN ARCHITECTURE MONOCULTURE AND THAT IS THE PLATEAU. All six of our members are facebook/dinov2-small at 336 px with one head (cls_mean token pool, max slice pool, attend slot pool), one six-slot list, whole_stack=True, backbone_lr=4e-5; only slices (12/20), band and a single through_plane flag vary. Seven differently-seated entries span 0.937-0.941 against a 0.0053 Hanley-McNeil floor because they are seven reseatings of one lens. The +0.002 here is below the 1.5 percent bar as a SCORE and is not a finding, but it is the first non-flat reading in twelve on ensemble construction, and the axis it moved is the one the pool never varied. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-28_architecture-monoculture.md.

ALL-OURS BEATS GRAFTED. Five of ours plus twenty CC0 members scored 0.894 against this entry's 0.925 on the same hidden set, and the offline holdout agreed in sign and under-priced the penalty. A published member fitted elsewhere is not a free member.

WHOLE-STACK, overlap=False. Averaging overlapping three-slice windows is another way of showing the model every slice, which a whole-stack member already does in feature space: +0.0146 for a windowed member, nothing here.

NOT FOUR MEMBERS - FIVE, AND THE FIFTH MUST BE STRONG. This entry retires the 'FOUR MEMBERS' principle every champion before it carried. That principle was read off a board where member COUNT and member QUALITY were perfectly confounded: every entry at or above 0.927 named four, and the only five- and six-member entries (crossenc 0.926, maxdiv 0.925) had each added an individually WEAK member (0.8268, 0.8345, taken 16th and 15th by greedy over eighteen). This entry holds the count at five and moves only the quality - base_dense at 0.8512, taken 7th - and it moved 0.930 to 0.931. So the four ticks crossenc and maxdiv lost were paid for member quality, not for the seat count, and the earlier 'falls monotonically past five' reading was a statement about the pool that was available then, not about ensemble size.

EVERY SHIPPED MEMBER IS FINGERPRINT-CHECKED AND WITNESS-CHECKED. A member fitted with --slice-pooling max and rebuilt with default channel stacking differs by 2.25 against a 2e-3 tolerance: a different function on different pixels, which loads and scores without complaint.

MEMBERSHIP WAS NOT EXHAUSTED, which the previous champion's own principles claimed. This entry is one named swap off that one - res392_ws out, band_dense in, same count and same two decode groups - and it moved 0.925 to 0.928. The claim was made after four swaps bought +0.007 with the third breaking the ordering rule; what was actually exhausted was the pool at the time, and band_dense is a member from an axis (the sampled BAND) that pool did not contain.

A MEMBER THAT FAILED ITS OWN MATCHED CONTROL CAN STILL WIN A SEAT. calib_span was written up as a failure hours before this entry: -0.0020 against its control at the settled operating point, on the arm that PROVED a lever's sign is a property of its operating point. It is the member that took this entry past 0.928. Member quality measured alone and seat value in a four-member vote are different quantities, and the alone-ordering here is INVERTED against the seat-ordering: alone band_span 0.8565 > depth_regions_narrow 0.8554 > calib_span 0.8545, in this seat calib_span 0.8670 > band_span 0.8661 > depth_regions_narrow 0.8653. Never retire a member on its own control alone; score it in the seat.

AN OFFLINE EDGE INSIDE THE NOISE FLOOR CAN STILL MOVE THE BOARD, and four occupants of ONE seat is what shows it. calib_span (+0.0022 offline over the champion, a third of the 0.0062 floor) is the only one of four that moved the board, and it moved it up a tick. The order agrees at the TOP - highest offline seat value, highest board - and inverts in the MIDDLE: band_span ranked second offline and last on the board. So the offline ruler picks the winner and does not resolve the field, which is a weaker tool than a full ordering and a much stronger one than nothing.

THE OFFLINE MAXIMUM IS A SUPPORTED MOVE, and this entry is the point that earned it. greedy4 was pre-registered at or below 0.929 with a stated refutation - above 0.929 would mean the greedy search finds board-real improvements at separations the seat experiment says it cannot resolve - and it landed 0.930, so the refutation fired against the ledger's own prediction. Five entries now pair an offline joint-holdout score with a board score: 0.8648/0.928, 0.8653/0.928, 0.8661/0.927, 0.8670/0.929, 0.8679/0.930. Four of the five are monotone and the single inversion is oneswap, whose entering member band_span is IN this entry and did not hurt it - so that inversion was a property of that four, not of the member. The previous principle stands but is now too weak as written: the ruler does not merely pick the winner, it orders the field at 4/5 over a 0.003 offline spread. Read it as a ranking tool with one known failure, and keep firing its maximum.

A DIFFERENT ENCODER IS WORTH A SEAT ITS OWN CONTROL SAYS IT LOST. base_dense peaked at 0.8512 against its matched control band_dense's 0.8578 - minus 0.0066, OUTSIDE the 0.0062 floor, at 2.5x the epoch cost. On its own ruler the bigger encoder LOST and the arm reads as a kill. Mixed into this seat it took the board up a tick. That is the calib_span lesson at a second point and on a stronger axis: alone-quality and seat-value are different quantities, and here the member that lost its control is the only DINOv2-base in a pool seven small members deep, so what it brought was error structure the other four do not have rather than accuracy they lack.

THE BATCH CONFOUND THIS ENTRY NAMED WAS MEASURED, NOT ARGUED AWAY. base_dense trained at --batch 6 because 336 px x 20 slices x 768 wide does not fit in 32 GB at 12, so its solo number carried a second variable it did not choose. batch_teardown ran the control's own recipe at batch 6 on the encoder where 12 IS affordable: 0.8598 against the control's 0.8578, +0.0020, inside the floor and on the positive side. The batch is not a lever at this operating point, so the minus 0.0066 is an ENCODER reading and this entry's 0.931 is not a batch artefact. Pre-register the confound, then spend card-time removing it - a verdict written while a named suspect is still unmeasured is a verdict that has to be re-litigated.

THE OFFLINE RULER PREDICTED A TIE AND THE BOARD PAID A TICK, which is the ruler's first miss in the UP direction. Offline the five read 0.8690 against the four's 0.8691 - minus 0.0001, predicting about minus 0.0003 under the 3x harm-multiplier slots 7-8 established - and the board returned plus 0.001. Six entries now pair the two rulers: 0.8648/0.928, 0.8653/0.928, 0.8661/0.927, 0.8670/0.929, 0.8679/0.930, 0.8691/0.930, 0.8690/0.931. The monotone reading survives everywhere except this last pair, where the offline order INVERTS against the board. Read it as: the 909-study holdout ranks the field but cannot resolve a 0.0001 separation, and a member that is offline-flat but structurally different is exactly the case where it will be wrong. Keep firing the offline maximum; stop treating an offline tie as a reason not to fire.

THE EDGE THAT PRODUCED IT WAS +0.0009 OFFLINE, a seventh of the 0.0062 noise floor, and the ledger argued that away twice before the entry ran. Two swaps compounded, one of them bringing the worst-transferring member, an edge shrunk by two thirds when the champion improved under it - every one of those was true and the entry still took the board. One board tick is this competition's reporting resolution so 0.930 over 0.929 is 'better', not 'much better'; what does NOT survive is the habit of declining to fire an offline maximum because its margin is small.

THE SEAT COUNT IS NOT THE VARIABLE - THE SEVENTH MEMBER'S TYPE OF DISTANCE IS. Five entries hold the same six members, the same kit and the same blend and move only who sits seventh: a near-twin of a seated member scored 0.930, a recipe-distant member 0.931, an OBJECTIVE-distant member (grade_ladder, the severity loss) 0.931, and this entry's PIXEL-distant member (through_dense, the only one whose input tensor differs) 0.932. Objective distance ties, pixel distance ticks. The ledger had already concluded from the first four rows that 'a seventh seat is worth 0.000 regardless of which member fills it' and withdrawn this entry on that basis; the conclusion generalised from one seventh member to all of them and this entry refutes it. Buy a seat on the axis, not on the count and not on the solo score.

+0.001 IS AN INSTRUMENT READING, NOT A RESULT, and this pin says so in its own record. One board increment is a sixth of the 0.0062 holdout floor and nothing against the 1.5% house bar or the 0.054 frontier gap. What it licenses is a DIRECTION - the decode-group argument of knee-7d1, whose 2.4x transfer is the same pixel axis measured offline - not a number to plan around.

A PIN THAT LAGS THE BOARD SILENTLY MISPRICES EVERY CANDIDATE UNDER IT. This entry scored at 02:45 UTC and the pin still named basedense_v1 three hours later, so seat_value - which reads the roster from here precisely so no arm header can hold a stale copy - would have priced the day's candidates against a five-member champion that no longer holds the board. champion_check asserts the pinned entry can be REBUILT; it cannot know the entry is still the best one. Update the pin in the same motion as reading the board.

THE ORDINAL RULER IS THE ONE THAT TRANSFERS, and this entry is its first honest forward test. It is one named swap off sevenplane - depth_regions_narrow out, grade_ladder in - chosen because grade_ladder leads on ordinal concordance by +0.007 over labels and +0.011 over pairs, and pre-registered on knee-7d1 before the number: above 0.932 confirms the ordinal ruler, 0.932 ties, below refutes it. It read 0.933. The other two rulers pointed elsewhere on the SAME swap: binary seat value priced it +0.0001, a fifteenth of its own +0.0015 resolution, and residual distance called grade_ladder the most redundant member of all 23 for its strength and predicted a LOSS. Rank seats by ordinal concordance; stop using residual distance as a selection rule, which has now failed twice in one day in opposite directions. One trial cannot separate 'the ruler transfers' from 'grade_ladder is a good member', so the next use of it is a RE-TEST, not an assumption.

AN OFFLINE SEAT NUMBER IS NOT A BOARD NUMBER UNTIL IT IS MULTIPLIED. This entry's entering member priced +0.0001 offline and bought +0.001 on the board. Hours earlier the same seat scan priced 63 candidates at +0.0005 or less and an interpretation concluded from that that the trained pool was EXHAUSTED - by comparing offline deltas straight against the +0.0015 threshold at which the board has been seen to tick. That comparison is a units error: board_transfer measures the compression, and an offline seat must be multiplied by it before it meets a board threshold. The pool is FLAT, not empty, and a seat ruler whose whole live range across 63 candidates is a third of its own resolution cannot say which candidate carries the tick. Never read an offline seat against a board threshold without the compression. CORRECTED 2026-08-24: this text read +4.67 board points per holdout point, fitted over five or six pairs spanning 0.0043 offline -- inside our own 0.0062 noise floor, so a slope through noise. The weakseven instrument (0.8562 offline, 0.908 board) placed a point outside that band and the refit reads +2.14. The best available eighth seat therefore prices at about +0.001 board, not +0.002, and every offline delta priced under the old constant is worth 46% of what it was sold for. The RULE stands; the CONSTANT halved. Read it from the tool, never from prose.

RETRACTED 2026-08-23, THE SAME DAY IT WAS WRITTEN. This slot held 'THE POOL IS THE VARIABLE, NOT THE ARRANGEMENT OF IT', argued from six entries reading 0.933, 0.933, 0.933, 0.932 and this one's 0.934: the four rearrangements tied, the one contents change ticked up, therefore the axis was real. That is a multiple-comparisons error and it is not a subtle one. The board resolves about 0.001. One entry landing one tick above four others across six tries is what noise produces, and calling the tick an AXIS while conceding the SIZE was directional does not rescue it - the axis claim rests entirely on the same one tick. The error was compounded by using it to reprice a ~10 h arm (knee-tfj3). What is actually established by these six entries is NOTHING about which axis pays; what remains established independently is that greedy7's +0.0018 offline edge sat inside a +0.0033 selection overfit, which forbids firing on offline maxima but licenses no axis in exchange. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-23_selection-overfit-explains-greedy7.md.

NO DIFFERENCE UNDER 0.02 IS A RESULT HERE - the owner's bar, restated 2026-08-23, and it governs this file. Applied honestly it says every entry in this project's history is one draw from the same distribution: the board span across all shipped entries is 0.930-0.937, the gap to the leaderboard leader is whatever comp/leaderboard.json last read (`python -m kneemri.kaggle.board_read --live`, and champion_check refuses a read over two days old) - this line carried 0.008, then 0.015, and decayed silently both times because nothing here read the board; the number is now a command, so do not quote one here again, and each is well inside the bar. So no principle in this list may be argued from a board DELTA. What a board reading can still do is refute an ABSOLUTE claim (a kernel that fails to build, a member that cannot load, an entry that collapses) and confirm that a shipped path works at all. Corollary for slot spending: a submission is a verification that the pipeline runs end to end, not a measurement of a method, and it must be priced that way.

A MEMBER FITTED AT --fold -1 IS UNSCOREABLE FOREVER, and this pin holds one. final_ws_e12 held out nothing, so it has seen every holdout study: it can never be seat-scored, curve-scored or distance-scored, and no pool containing it may report an offline mean. Every future roster decision involving this entry is therefore made BLIND against whatever the board last said, which is a real cost of the data step and is recorded here rather than rediscovered when a scan silently includes it.

THE ALL-DATA AXIS IS REAL AND SUB-LINEAR, read as a DOSE and not as a one-off. Two entries hold count (7), vote (RankAverage) and serving fixed and move only how many seats trained on all 4,406 studies instead of 3,497: finalfit one seat 0.934, this entry six seats 0.937. The first seat bought about +0.001 over the 0.933 chain, the next five bought +0.003 together - roughly +0.0006 a seat against the first seat's +0.001. So the seats are NOT independent: six all-data members largely re-learn the same extra 909 studies. The consequence was pre-registered before the number in interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-24_the_all_data_dose_response.md, whose 0.936-0.939 band reads verbatim 'the 7.3 h train is NOT justified - the honest move is to stop here and record the axis as real-but-spent'. band_dense_long_ff is therefore UNRUN and the card stays with the other project. A band written before the read is the only thing that makes a +0.003 stopping point a decision rather than a story.

THIS PIN IS NEARLY BLIND, which is worse than the previous one and is the price of the axis that produced it. Six of its seven seats are --fold -1, so the entry has no offline number of any kind by construction - not a weak one, none. board.jsonl records its offline as null and board_transfer's own `unmeasured()` names it rather than dropping it silently. Every roster decision from here is made against the board alone at five reads a day, and the offline ruler can only be used on pools that exclude these six. Buying board points by spending the ability to measure offline is a trade that cannot be made twice.

A LEDGER THAT NOTHING READS GOES STALE SILENTLY, and it took four days and a pushed correction to notice. comp/board.jsonl - the machine-readable half that board_transfer prices EVERY experiment from - stopped being written on 2026-08-20 while comp/SUBMISSIONS.md kept its prose current, so seven entries (sevenplane, gradeswap, accumseat, greedy7, finalfit, weakseven, allfit) existed in the prose and not in the record. The 2026-08-24 refit was then computed by HAND from that prose and mis-paired gradeswap's offline 0.8694 with finalfit's board 0.934 - two different entries, because finalfit has no offline number at all - and the resulting +2.14 was written into this file AND into comp/members.roster as a correction. Backfilled, the tool itself reads +1.92 over 15 entries and 90 pairs. The rule that survives unchanged is the one that matters (never read an offline seat against a board threshold without the compression); the constant has now been wrong twice, first at +4.67 and then at +2.14, and both times because it was quoted from prose. Read it from `python -m kneemri.evaluation.board_transfer`, and if the two disagree the record is stale, not the tool.

THE INVERSION CLAUSE GOT STRONGER ON MORE DATA, which is the one place this project's ruler has held up. With the backfill the holdout inverts on 4 of 90 orderable pairs and 0 of the 57 it resolves at all - every disagreement still sits under the 0.0053 floor, now over 57 resolved pairs instead of 33. But note what the slope is fitted ON: the four best entries here (allfit, finalfit, sevenplane, accumseat) are ONE-SIDED and enter no pair, so +1.92 is measured entirely on entries at or below 0.933 and is an extrapolation at the top of the board. Trust the SIGN above 0.0053, halve the MAGNITUDE, and do not quote the slope as though it had been tested where we now live.

THE KIT SHA ON THIS PIN IS DIRTY, and it is the first one that is. Every pin before this read a bare seven-character sha off its kernel log; this entry's log says 'kit aa79cd3 DIRTY', so the sha names a commit the shipped bytes were not equal to. The DIRTY is recorded here rather than trimmed off, because a pin whose whole purpose is that the entry can be rebuilt must not claim a reproducibility it does not have: aa79cd3 plus unknown working-tree edits is what scored 0.938. farseat, shipped from the same dirty tree, carries the same marker in board.jsonl. This does not make the entry unbuildable - its members are named by its kernel and packaged by the roster, which is what champion_check asserts - it makes the SERVING CODE approximate. Ship the next entry from a clean tree, and if a dirty ship is unavoidable, the marker travels with it.

THIS PIN IS FULLY BLIND, where the previous one was nearly. allfit held one fold-0 seat (band_dense_long_s2026) among seven; this entry is those seven minus exactly that seat, so all six of its members were fitted at --fold -1 and every one of them has seen every holdout study. There is no pool here that can be seat-scored, curve-scored or distance-scored at all - not a weak offline number, none, and board.jsonl records offline null by construction. seat_value reads its roster from this pin, so the consequence is direct: priced against the champion it can report no offline mean whatsoever. The door that remains is seat_value --against <board entry>, which exists precisely because the champion stopped being scoreable, and it must now be pointed at an entry whose members are not all-data. Two pins in a row have bought board position by spending the ability to measure, and the second one spent the last of it.

THE PIN LAGGED A SECOND TIME, so the rule stopped being prose and became a check. The principle above states in this file that a lagging pin misprices every candidate under it and that the pin must be updated in the same motion as reading the board. It was written after basedense_v1 held the pin three hours past allfit's score - and then allfit held the pin while votefit_v1 sat on the board at 0.938, through five further submissions. A rule that has now failed twice in the same way is not a rule anyone is going to remember on the third occasion; knee-cun6 moves it into champion_check, which already reads board.jsonl and can simply compare. Note what the move does NOT rest on: 0.938 over 0.937 is one board tick, under the noise floor, and the record says plainly it is not a result. The pin is a reproducibility record of the best-scoring path, not a claim that the path is better - which is exactly why it can be kept current mechanically.

SUBSTITUTING A FOLD-0 TWIN TO SCORE THIS PIN PRODUCES A CONFIDENT WRONG ANSWER, which is worse than the blindness the two principles above record. Measured 2026-08-25: the five fold-0 twins of this entry's six members read 0.8687 offline, peak8_v1 reads 0.8731, so the offline ruler prices peak8 about eight board ticks ABOVE this entry at the measured +1.72 compression. The board reads peak8 0.932 against this entry's 0.938 - six ticks the other way, a fourteen-tick miss on a gap the holdout resolves, far outside the inversion clause (8/171 pairs, all under the 0.0053 floor). The mechanism is not a ruler failure: 0.8687 is the score of five DIFFERENT, WEAKER models fitted on 3,497 studies, not of this entry, and the all-data dose (+0.004 to +0.005) is a third of what would be needed to explain the gap - so the size of the boundary effect is UNKNOWN and larger than any offline delta this project can produce. The rule: an offline number may only be compared to another offline number fitted on the SAME studies, and there is no comparison across the --fold -1 line - not a weak one, not one with a correction applied, none. CORRECTED the same hour, against knee-97ib: I first read lastseat_v1's 0.937 against THIS entry's 0.938 and called a fold-0 seat a one-tick cost. That compares across a changed VOTE - this entry is dark6 with LogitAverage, and the matched control is dark6 itself at 0.937 - so the fold-0 seat is FLAT, and lastseat_v1 (fold-0) against dark7_v1 (the same member refit at --fold -1) is 0.937 both ways. What remains is the inert seventh seat, six rosters and one tick of spread, which withdraws a mixed candidate on a strong prior rather than on a measured loss. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-25_the-all-data-boundary.md.

THE CORPUS AXIS HAS A BOARD NUMBER NOW, AND IT IS ONE TICK. This entry is votefit's six with base_dense_ff replaced by merged_blend_s2026 - the only member this project owns that was fitted on external expert image reads (Rijeka) - with the vote rule, the count, the kit and the serving config all held, so the single moving variable is the CORPUS one seat saw. It read 0.939 against votefit's 0.938, inside its own pre-registered 0.939-0.941 band, which the kernel wrote as 'as predicted, and inside the noise'. One tick is under the 0.0062 paired floor and an order of magnitude under the house 1.5% bar, so nothing here is a result. What it establishes is narrow and was previously unowned: every merged-corpus number this project had was OFFLINE, and an externally-fitted member had never been shown to be safe at serving. It is now shown to be at worst neutral in a champion seat. It does NOT license the 7 h merged_blend_ff refit - that refit separates the two corpus mechanisms and would need its own band. Note also what this pin does to the blindness the two principles above record: five of six seats remain --fold -1, so the entry is still unscoreable as a pool, and swapping in a member that is not all-data does not buy the ability to measure it - a mixed pool cannot be compared across the --fold -1 line either.

IMPROVING EVERY SEAT AT ONCE DOES NOT COMPOUND, and this entry is what measured it. It is the previous pin's six seating with --calibrated-targets on all six seats - no seat moves, no member enters or leaves, the vote, count, serving views and member order are the champion's untouched - so the single variable is member QUALITY at roster scale, on the only term this project has measured positive twice (knee-bs4l: +0.0072 proxy / +0.0129 annotated at the span corner, +0.0061 at the dense-hold corner). It read 0.941, a new best and the first of twelve entries to leave the 0.936-0.939 plateau. It also came in BELOW its own pre-registration (knee-wrl6, ~0.944 with knee-ps8o's halved local slope already applied), and that miss is the finding: the 23% seat pass-through was measured for ADDING one member to a roster, and nothing had ever measured what happens when all six improve on the same axis together. The answer is that it does not improve - six simultaneous member gains pass through no better than one. READ THE +0.002 AS DIRECTIONAL: it is under the 0.0053 Hanley-McNeil floor and well under the 0.0062 three-seed floor, and one board read cannot separate it from the plateau it topped.
